_comment: Acknowledged-warning ledger (v3.28 zero-warning discipline). Each record silences exactly one check_run.py WARN that the weekly quality audit reviewed and judged unfixable without falsifying immutable history (run records are never edited after their fire; entries are immutable). warn() reclassifies a warning as ACK when record.check equals the check label and record.match is a substring of the message — pin `match` to the specific run/subject so nothing else is ever swallowed. Only the weekly quality audit (or an operator-directed session) adds records, never a run for its own fresh warnings; every addition names its reason and date and appears in the commit diff for review.

Reviewed by the 2026-07-26 weekly quality audit and judged unfixable: every Sonnet (cti-verification-alt) spawn in that fire terminated on the content-safety classifier — iteration 2 was retried and failed again, as did three of four research spawns — so no other-model confirmation pass was available. The run recorded the blocked-spawn exception in verification.confirmation_waived exactly as the policy requires, and both confirming iterations were genuine independent CLEAN passes; only the two-DIFFERENT-models requirement was waived. The record is immutable, so nothing can change it. Deliberately NOT fixed in code: teaching check_run.py to auto-pass a same-model confirmation whenever confirmation_waived is non-null would let any future run silence the rotation check by writing its own waiver text, which is the self-serve mute button the discipline forbids and a weakening of hard invariant #11. The warning did its job — it surfaced for review, and this ledger record is the review.

acknowledged.reason: Reviewed by the 2026-08-02 weekly quality audit and judged unfixable. The 2026-07-26 audit ran four full cold-read passes alternating Opus and Sonnet (the rotation held), remediated all 30 findings they produced, and confirmed the last two partial applications in a fifth, scoped pass that returned CLEAN. Because that CLEAN was scoped rather than a full cold read, and the run stood at ~2.5 h with the publishing chain still ahead, the wall-clock watchdog took precedence over a sixth full pass — which is the watchdog working as designed, not a gate being skipped. The run record documents exactly what was and was not established, in the run's own words. Run records are immutable, so nothing can change it, and the binding constraint was wall clock rather than the 8-iteration cap, so no cap change would have prevented it. Deliberately NOT fixed in code: the check must keep firing on an unconfirmed final CLEAN regardless of how well-reasoned the waiver text is, because auto-passing on a non-null confirmation_waived would let any run mute the double-CLEAN gate with its own prose.

Reviewed by the 2026-08-02 weekly quality audit and judged unfixable. The fire ran the full 8 iterations with a perfect Opus/Sonnet rotation and no same-model consecutive pair; iteration 8 (Sonnet) returned CLEAN following a NEEDS_FIXES at 7, so the cap left no room for the confirming other-model pass. That is the designed fail-open, correctly recorded in verification.confirmation_waived, and it is era-correct under the v3.27 cap. The record is immutable. Deliberately NOT fixed by raising the cap: this window's mean was 6.6 iterations and four of nine fires reached a genuine two-model confirmed CLEAN inside the cap, so the cap is converging for most fires; raising it again would trade publish latency for a marginal case rather than fix a systemic one. The audit's own review of the four entries this fire published found no defect the extra pass would have caught — all four were verified clean by batch B4 of this audit's retrospective truth passes.

Reviewed by the 2026-08-09 weekly quality audit and judged correct as published. The check's own wording carves this out — 'unless the piece genuinely carries no TTP content' — and this piece genuinely does not: it reports that NCSC-NL and BSI CERT-Bund withdrew SQLite advisories whose CVEs were fabricated by an LLM, and that GHSA was still serving one of the withdrawn records. There is no attacker, no intrusion and no tradecraft anywhere in it; the subject is advisory-database quality control. The entry is immutable, and the only ways to clear the warning would be to invent a mapping for behaviour no source describes — the exact hallucination the v3.30 evidence floor forbids, and worse than the warning — or to weaken the check for every research entry. Deliberately NOT fixed in code: research-kind empty techniques[] must keep WARNing, because the common case is a real mapping omission and only a human-reviewed exception like this one should pass.

Reviewed by the 2026-08-09 weekly quality audit and judged unfixable. The previous audit fire ran the full 8 iterations with a perfect Opus/Sonnet rotation and no same-model consecutive pair; iteration 6 (Sonnet) returned CLEAN, iteration 7 (Opus) refused it and was right to — it caught a sourcing_note that had inverted its own finding about an authority's reachability — and iteration 8 (Sonnet) verified that repair independently. The cap then left no room for the confirming other-model pass. That is the designed fail-open, correctly recorded in verification.confirmation_waived, and the record is immutable. This audit's retrospective truth passes re-verified that fire's five published entries against primary sources. Deliberately NOT fixed by raising the cap: this window's confirmed-CLEAN rate fell to 2 of 12 with a mean of 5.8 iterations, and the binding problem is convergence rather than headroom — v3.31's model-override ladder addresses the cause (fires losing two-model agreement to blocked alternate spawns) instead of buying a ninth pass.

Reviewed by the 2026-08-09 weekly quality audit and judged unfixable. This was a duplicate-week stand-down whose verifier loop ran against a run record and nothing else, and it earned its eight iterations: it removed three fabricated or inverted telemetry claims (a completed timestamp that had not yet occurred, an inverted coverage-gap assertion, a source status change that never happened), two unsourced quantifiers, and — after iteration 4 returned CLEAN and iteration 5 refused to confirm it — two substantive factual errors, including an AI Act timetable that was wrong three separate times before the paraphrase was abandoned for a verbatim quotation. Iteration 7 refuted the run's own headline operator finding. The final CLEAN at iteration 8 is unconfirmed only because iteration 7 was NEEDS_FIXES and the cap left no room; the waiver records it and the record is immutable. Deliberately NOT fixed in code: the check must keep firing on an unconfirmed final CLEAN however well-reasoned the waiver, or any run could mute the double-CLEAN gate with its own prose.

Container-lifetime artifact on an immutable record, reviewed by the 2026-08-30 quality audit. The fire started 2026-08-21T04:10Z and its record was completed 2026-08-24T09:00Z: the container stalled for roughly three days and the run was finished on 08-24, so the 76.8 h is elapsed container lifetime, not work. The 2026-08-24 audit root-caused the surrounding measurement problem (through v3.31 `completed` was stamped in Phase 5, before the verifier loop) and shipped the fix that moved the stamp to Phase 6; from v3.32 on the value is honest wall clock, which is exactly why this record now reads long. Run records are immutable and the duration is a historical fact. Deliberately NOT fixed in code: the runaway check must keep firing on a long duration, because the common case is a genuine overrun and only a reviewed exception like this one should pass.

Same container-stall class as 2026-08-21T0410Z-intel, reviewed by the 2026-08-30 quality audit: started 2026-08-22T04:10Z, record completed 2026-08-24T09:20Z. The run's own verification note states it plainly — 'the 53 h in duration_seconds is elapsed container lifetime, not work', against about 4.75 h of active work. Immutable record, historical fact.

Era-correct recorded fail-open, reviewed by the 2026-08-30 quality audit. Iteration 3 returned CLEAN after roughly 4.75 h of active work against the ~3 h wall-clock guard whose instruction is to land rather than widen, so the confirming pass was waived and the gate recorded as NOT met, in the run's own words, with the waiver text naming what the run does and does not carry in its place. That is the watchdog working as designed, not a gate skipped. The record is immutable. Deliberately NOT fixed in code: auto-passing an unconfirmed CLEAN whenever `confirmation_waived` is non-null would let any run mute the double-CLEAN gate with its own prose.

Reviewed by the 2026-08-30 quality audit and judged settled history. The record's own S-agent note documents the cause: a container stall put the fire on top of the 09:00 UTC embargo lift for the Swiss half-year threat report, and the main agent re-tasked a sub-agent mid-flight to catch that publication minutes after it went live. The 11.3 h is elapsed container lifetime around a stall, and the run turned it into coverage rather than losing it. Immutable record.

Reviewed by the 2026-08-30 quality audit and judged settled history: the audit fire of 2026-08-24 booted on a container clock reading 2026-08-16 with an eight-day-stale clone, detected and corrected the skew mid-run, and completed the same evening. The 11.5 h spans that detection and re-plan on a stalling container, not a runaway workload; v3.34's Phase 0 step 0 clock/clone cross-check shipped in direct response. Immutable record.

Reviewed by the 2026-08-30 quality audit and judged the watchdog working as designed. The fire's own verification note explains the 3.5 h in full: a 91 h catch-up window and 36 published entries produced a long verifier tail, the run crossed the ~3 h mark after iteration 5, and per anti-crash guard #10 iteration 6 was run as the final one so the run landed instead of widening. The record documents the overrun and its cause exactly as the guard requires. Immutable record, historical fact.

Reviewed by the 2026-08-30 quality audit: the 7.2 h is the wall clock of an operator-interactive session, not an unattended fire. The 2026-08-28 record is an operator-directed editorial review conducted with a human in the loop on a read-only-git sandbox, where elapsed time tracks the operator's own review pace across four verifier iterations and a 39-entry editorial pass. The runaway threshold is calibrated for autonomous fires and does not describe this shape. Immutable record. Deliberately NOT fixed in code: exempting `kind: audit` or a human-in-the-loop flag from the runaway check would blind it to a genuinely runaway audit fire, which is the case it exists for.

Era-correct recorded fail-open, reviewed by the 2026-08-30 quality audit. Iterations 1-3 each caught genuine remediation gaps and iteration 4 returned CLEAN with zero findings; the confirming pass was waived because the session was operator-interactive on a sandbox with no external network, so a fifth no-network pass would have added no new evidence class, and the operator reviewed the complete working-tree diff before committing. The waiver names both grounds on the record. The URL-level re-verification it deferred was carried out by this audit's retrospective truth passes over all 39 touched entries, so the substantive gap the waiver left open is now closed. The record itself is immutable. Deliberately NOT fixed in code: the check must keep firing on an unconfirmed final CLEAN however well-reasoned the waiver, or any run could mute the double-CLEAN gate with its own prose.
